To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a novel training scheme with a set of novel losses named moment reconstruction loss is proposed for conditional GANs, (2) our training scheme can be applied to any conditional GANs and (3) our approach achieves a great diversity in generated samples while maintaining or even improving the fidelity of samples.

(i) the joint use of GAN loss with reconstruction loss leads to lack of diversity in generated samples and (ii) our proposed training scheme with moment reconstruction losses achieves both training stability and output diversity.
we propose novel training methods with a new set loss for conditional image generation tasks that can generate diverse outputs while maintaining the visual quality of the outputs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to achieve multimodal conditional generation, which is an important and challenging topic in computer vision.
how to achieve both training stability and output diversity in conditional GAN models.

the following questions: (1) Can we improve the training stability and the diversity of conditional GANs without losing visual fidelity? (2) Can we achieve the above goals with a simple modification of the training scheme and the loss function?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method achieves a great trade-off between the diversity of output samples and the quality of the visual fidelity of the generated samples.
our method is able to produce diverse and visually appealing outputs while keeping the training stable.

our method achieves the best of both worlds, that is, it generates diverse outputs with high fidelity. A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our approach can be used as a plug-in module to replace the reconstruction loss, and can be easily incorporated into any conditional GAN model.

we provide a novel training recipe for conditional image generation tasks by replacing the reconstruction loss with a set of moment reconstruction losses, which enables the generation of more diverse samples while preserving the visual fidelity of the outputs.

our approach enables the GAN models to achieve both training stability and diversity in output generation, which are two critical issues that have been long unsolved in the field of conditional image generation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GAN loss alone can be a sufficient loss function for conditional image generation, which has been overlooked in previous works.
the reconstruction loss, which has long been considered as a standard loss in conditional image generation, should be replaced with a more suitable loss function for the task.
the reconstruction loss is not a necessary component for conditional generation tasks and that it should be replaced with the moment reconstruction loss in order to obtain more diverse outputs.
